newsitem.title: USA: High water closes more locks on Mississippi River.
newsitem.headline: High water closes more locks on Mississippi River.

text.p: High water forced more lock closures on the Mississippi River near Pleasant Valley, Iowa, and southward, the Coast Guard said.

"Lock and Dam 14, Pleasant Valley, Iowa, through Lock and Dam 17, New Boston, Ill., are closed effective Wednesday," said Bob Hildebrand, chief warrant officer, Coast Guard Marine Safety Office at St Louis.
Lock and Dam 13 at Fulton, Illinois was closed a few days ago, he said.
As of Wednesday, there were no plans to close Lock and Dam 18, Gladstone, Ill., through Lock and Dam 20 at Canton, Mo. "But that is subject to change," he said.
Locks from from upper and lower St Anthony Falls, Minn., down to New Boston, Ill., were now shut down. "It is a waterways management issue," Hildebrand said.

Commerce was affected but traffic was thin. "As of today (Wednesday) I have 12 vessels upbound from Lock 13 north that are stuck in between the locks and 24 vessels southbound that cannot travel downriver," Hildebrand said. But he stressed that was considered light traffic.
The Coast guard also issued Wednesday another safety advisory from River Mile 168.6 Jefferson Barracks Bridge, southern part of St Louis, up to Mile 218 at Grafton, Ill.
High water and fast currents have created hazardous conditions for vessels operating in fleeting areas which are like parking lots for barges, he said.
"That is in effect until the flood stage at St Louis goes below 25 feet. It is now at 29.2 feet, just below flood stage at 30 feet," Hildebrand said.
Asked when operations were expected to get back to normal, Hildebrand replied, it was "unknown" and too early to assess.
"When the water gets down to near flood stage or below in those areas, things will get back to normal," he said.
